3.title: Beginner's Mindfulness — Part 1
3.body:
**Module 1: The Breath as Anchor**

Sit comfortably. Close your eyes. Bring your attention to the sensation of breathing — the cool air entering your nostrils, the gentle rise of your chest. Don't try to change anything. Just notice.

When your mind wanders (and it will), gently return to the breath. This is the practice — not staying focused, but returning.

Try this for 2 minutes today. Tomorrow, try 3.

**Module 2: Body Scan**

Lie down or sit comfortably. Starting at the crown of your head, slowly move your attention down through your body — forehead, jaw, neck, shoulders, arms, hands, chest, belly, hips, legs, feet.

Notice any tension, warmth, tingling, or numbness. Don't judge. Just observe.

This is your first lesson in embodied awareness.

5.title: 4-4-4 Box Breathing
5.subtitle: The Navy SEAL technique for calm
5.body:
Box breathing is used by Navy SEALs, first responders, and meditators alike. It activates the parasympathetic nervous system — your body's natural brake pedal.

**How it works:**

1. **Inhale** through your nose for 4 seconds
2. **Hold** your breath for 4 seconds
3. **Exhale** slowly through your mouth for 4 seconds
4. **Hold** empty for 4 seconds

Repeat 4 times. Feel the shift.

Try this before difficult conversations, before sleep, or anytime you feel your nervous system running the show.

9.title: Beginner's Mindfulness — Part 2
9.body:
**Module 3: Labeling Thoughts**

Sit quietly. When a thought arises, silently label it: 'planning,' 'worrying,' 'remembering,' 'judging.' Then let it go, like a leaf floating downstream.

**Module 4: Walking Meditation**

Walk slowly, deliberately. Feel each foot touch the ground — heel, ball, toes. Match your breath to your steps. The world becomes your meditation cushion.

**Module 5: Mindful Eating**

Choose one meal today. Eat slowly. Notice colors, textures, temperatures, flavors. Put your fork down between bites. This is presence.

12.title: Yoga Foundations — Part 1
12.body:
**Module 1: Mountain Pose (Tadasana)**

Stand with feet hip-width apart. Root down through all four corners of your feet. Lift your kneecaps, engage your thighs, lengthen your spine. Crown of the head reaches toward the sky.

**Module 2: Cat-Cow (Marjaryasana-Bitilasana)**

On hands and knees. Inhale: drop belly, lift gaze (Cow). Exhale: round spine, tuck chin (Cat). Flow with your breath for 2 minutes.

**Module 3: Child's Pose (Balasana)**

Knees wide, big toes touching. Fold forward, forehead to the ground. Arms extended or resting alongside. Breathe into your back body. Surrender.

16.title: Beginner's Mindfulness — Part 3
16.body:
**Module 6: Loving-Kindness (Metta)**

Sit quietly. Picture yourself. Silently repeat: 'May I be happy. May I be healthy. May I be safe. May I live with ease.'

Now picture someone you love. Same phrases. Then a neutral person. Then someone you find difficult. Finally, all beings everywhere.

**Module 7: Open Awareness**

Don't focus on anything. Don't push anything away. Let sounds, sensations, thoughts come and go like clouds across a vast sky. You are the sky — not the clouds.

19.title: Breathwork Essentials — Part 1
19.body:
**Module 1: Diaphragmatic Breathing**

Lie on your back, one hand on belly, one on chest. Breathe so the belly hand rises while the chest hand stays still. This is how you breathed as a baby. Relearn it now.

**Module 2: 4-7-8 Breathing**

Inhale 4 seconds. Hold 7 seconds. Exhale 8 seconds (through mouth, making a whoosh sound). 4 cycles max. This is a natural tranquilizer for the nervous system.

23.title: Yoga Foundations — Part 2
23.body:
**Module 4: Downward Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana)**

Hands shoulder-width, feet hip-width. Hips lift toward the sky. Pedal out your feet. This is both a resting pose and a strength builder.

**Module 5: Warrior I (Virabhadrasana I)**

Step one foot forward, bend the front knee. Back leg straight, heel grounded. Arms reach up. Gaze forward. Feel the power in stillness.

**Module 6: Tree Pose (Vrksasana)**

Shift weight to one foot. Place the other foot on your ankle, calf, or inner thigh (never the knee). Hands at heart center or reaching up. Find your balance.

**Module 7: Savasana**

Lie flat on your back. Arms slightly away from body, palms up. Legs relaxed, feet falling open. Let go completely. Stay 5-10 minutes. This is the hardest pose.

26.title: Lofi & Deep Focus — Part 1
26.body:
**Module 1: The Science of Focus Music**

Lo-fi's imperfections — vinyl crackle, tape hiss, slight pitch variations — create what neuroscientists call 'stochastic resonance.' Your brain leans in to fill the gaps, increasing attention.

**Module 2: Creating Your Sound Environment**

Choose your anchor sound. Some prefer pure instrumental. Others need nature layers — rain, waves, forest ambience. Experiment. Your nervous system will tell you what's right.

**Module 3: The Pomodoro Flow**

25 minutes of deep work with Lofi. 5 minutes of silence or nature sounds. Repeat 4 times. Then take a longer break. Notice how music shapes your attention rhythm.
